open_points.subject: Import confirmation after an identical re-upload
open_points.text: A16 says another upload replaces the uploaded file, “one of the same bytes included,” and requires confirmation after that replacement to be refused; but M11 records only the uploaded file, while A13 binds the confirmation to the file’s digest and A16 says it “applies the file of that digest.” No upload occurrence, generation or other fact distinguishes two uploads of identical bytes.
open_points.question: How does Registry determine that the particular upload for which confirmation was shown has been replaced when the replacement has identical bytes and therefore the same digest?
options: Treat each upload occurrence as distinct and retain some occurrence value until confirmation
Treat identical bytes as the same confirmed file, allowing the existing confirmation
Use an unstated runtime identity of the uploaded object to distinguish occurrences
open_points.default_guess: Treat every successful upload as a new occurrence and invalidate the pending confirmation even when its bytes and digest are identical.

witness.initial: The import is open. One valid owner session has uploaded file F, viewed its mapping, and received confirmation value C bound to digest D and fixed picks and mapping inputs.
events: The owner uploads F again in the same session with exactly the same bytes; A16 says this replaces the earlier upload.
The owner submits C with the same picks and mapping inputs.
outcomes: A16 rule 2 and required test 3 refuse the submission because the file for which C was shown is no longer kept, even though the new file has the same bytes.
A13 rule 6 accepts the binding because the current file still has digest D and the inputs match; A16 then applies the currently kept file of that digest and the import commits.
witness.observer: The owner sees refusal versus successful import, and the production store either remains unchanged or gains the imported records and migration closure.
